errors: internet outage 14:35Z-19:01Z (see coverage_gaps); both Monitor clocks kept ticking but the agent could not reach the API
lessons: Fill-arming rule works: FRMI stop armed at 08:24 with last 6.91 < trigger 7.27 filled AT 7.27 on the fresh 12:51Z cross - backtest fill-at-the-cross semantics preserved (vs Day 5's LFST -1.6% sweep). Fill-realism still -1.1% vs +60s because the break itself faded; that is adverse selection of premarket breaks, not order mechanics.
Thin-book veto saved a chase again: FF's 6.63 break (11:31Z) ran to 6.70 and collapsed to 6.21; the 0.5% spread veto + already-met-trigger rule kept us out. Veto save #1 of Day 6.

The halal gate removed the day's entire top tier: WXM +153% (EOD), FRTT +117% (loans 34%), BW +35%, PLUG +14%, ACB, RPD, ~35 total rejects. 8 live screens run same-day (FENC PASS, FRTT/ASTC/BHST/BGDE/EXYN/TC FAIL, AIAI unverifiable).

Sequential rotation's cost surfaces on outage days: one mid-pack position (FRMI +18-24% mover) held the sole ticket while KOPN ran to +29-30% on the bench; the one-position rule is by design, but a real broker's resting orders would also have kept us in FRMI - the sim behaved exactly like the architecture.

Resting-order architecture is outage-proof by construction: the stop (6.6884) and flatten rules were fully specified at arm time, so a 4.5-hour monitoring blackout could be settled deterministically from the tape with zero discretion. This is the strongest argument yet for broker-resident orders over loop-layer decisions.

Machine-level single point of failure: both Monitor clocks survived (they run locally) but every API call died with the internet. A future hardening: a broker-side OCO (stop + time-based flatten) would make even the settlement step unnecessary.
